name: Obadiah

facts.author: Obadiah, whose name means "servant of the LORD" (1:1). Nothing else is known about him for certain.
facts.audience: The people of Judah, given as a message about the nation of Edom

about: Obadiah is the shortest book of the Old Testament, only twenty-one verses long. It is a vision about Edom, the nation that came from Esau, the twin brother of Jacob. Edom lived in the high, rocky mountains south-east of the Dead Sea and felt safe there (1:3).

When enemies attacked Jerusalem, the Edomites did not help their brother Jacob. They stood by and watched, rejoiced at Judah's trouble, carried off goods and even handed over those who tried to escape (1:10-14). So God declares that proud Edom will be brought down, and what it has done will come back on its own head (1:15).
The book ends with hope for God's people. On mount Zion there will be deliverance and holiness, the house of Jacob will possess its land again, and the kingdom will belong to the LORD (1:21).

themes.title: Pride goes before a fall
themes.text: Edom trusted in its high rocks and its wise men, but God would bring it down.

themes.title: Caring for a brother
themes.text: Edom is judged for its violence and for rejoicing when its brother nation suffered.

themes.title: God's justice
themes.text: In the day of the LORD, each nation will receive what it has done to others.

themes.title: The kingdom is the LORD's
themes.text: God will save His people on mount Zion and rule over all.
